description_en: Twostūpasfrom approx. 14th-15th century.The village of Garjyāṅkoṭa is located 8 km east of Khalaṅgā (Jumla Bajār). Thestūpasare found on the southern slope of Garjyāṅkoṭa's western hill. It is on land owned by Jay Bahadur Bhandari, Tuka Bhahadur Bhandari and Bhim Bahadur Bhandari.The twostūpasare built next to one another. The monuments are built of carved stone blocks. The soil below it was collapsing. It has recently been consolidated with a retaining wall made of roughly cut stones. A stone fountain (mugrāhā,dhārā) was originally built below thestūpas. It is locally said that water stopped coming to the fountain after a woman who was menstruating took water from it.The monuments are stylistically similar to the ones found in the nearby village of Bigare (JUM0010), that can be dated from the 14th-15th century. Thestūpasin Garjyāṅkoṭa can thus be dated from the same period. This time period corresponds to the end of the Khaśa Malla kingdom (12th-14th century) and the beginning of the Kalyāl dynasty's rule from Jumla (15th century) (Andolfatto 2019).
monument_assessment: Slightly damaged (minor damages such as minor cracks, plants, missing stones in plinths), Rebuilt, Repaired , Restored
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. 2019. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne Université.
